- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to match mean reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and overpredicts; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 days to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.3) and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates upside; add 1–3% to forecast for next 5–7 days to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (0.1–0.3), model exhibits lag: forecast is typically 1–3 days behind true trend; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
- In low-sentiment environments (sentiment <0.1), model often underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to account for hidden volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–2% in final 5–7 days to reflect diminishing momentum.
